newsitem.title: ROMANIA: EX-SPY FACES TRIAL IN ROMANIA FOR TAPE LEAKS-MEDIA.
newsitem.headline: EX-SPY FACES TRIAL IN ROMANIA FOR TAPE LEAKS-MEDIA.

text.p: A former spy faces trial for disclosing classified information by making public telephone conversations alleged to have been tapped by Romania's intelligence agency, newspapers said on Saturday.

Captain Constantin Bucur, a former employee of the Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI), would be court-martialled on charges of "stealing from public assets, release of classified information and disclosing information on private persons", the daily Adevarul said.
Bucur faces charges of removing tapes from SRI headquarters and giving them to the media, the daily Cronica Romana said. If convicted, he could be sentenced to seven years in prison.
There were no officials available at the military prosecutors' office to comment on the reports.

Bucur is running for a seat in the lower house of parliament in next week's general election on the ticket of the hardline nationalist Greater Romania Party (PRM). If elected, he would secure immunity from prosecution enjoyed by all deputies.
The SRI is the successor to the pervasive Securitate of the communist era. Romanians believe the Securitate could listen in to almost anything and that the SRI inherited its technology.

Bucur was dismissed by the SRI this year after producing tapes at a news conference of what he said were illegal wire taps. The tapes featured mostly innocuous conversations by prominent politicians and journalists, including one politician chatting to his mother.
The head of the SRI, Virgil Magureanu, dismissed accusations of illegal bugging, saying that his agency always secured warrants when required.
A parliamentary committee has revealed almost 900 cases of authorised telephone tapping by the SRI last year alone, 80 percent of them against resident foreigners. REUTER
